messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert triggered: high error-rate observed on streaming/function-call pipeline (SSE) in prod-us-east-1. Rule: SSE >10% disconnects AND tool-call parse_errors >5%. Assigning oncall.

maria: I’m taking this. oncall runbook step 1 started — collecting logs + impacted customers list. @liam can you grab ingress proxy metrics?

liam: pulling nginx/access and envoy metrics now. early glance shows a spike in 11:23-11:28 UTC on 2131110000.

devon: I’m tailing runtime logs for tool-call path. Seeing repeated: `tool_call: parse_error: unexpected EOF while reading json` for requests with content-length small and SSE chunking. Also some `sse: connection reset by peer`.

maria: ok timeline note: root errors start ~11:22 UTC. Customers A and C reported degraded streaming completions at 11:25. Marking customer impact: partial failures for streaming tool-calls, fallback to non-streaming in some SDKs.

aj: posting quick log snippet from runtime (redacted):
```
[11:23:04] tool_call: req_id=0xabc123 payload=\"{\"tool\":\"search\",\"args\":\"...\"\" 
[11:23:04] parser: unexpected EOF while parsing JSON fragment
[11:23:04] sse: connection closed by client (remote=10.2.4.12:52344)
```

maria: thanks. hypothesis 1: client SDK change in 2.14.x that switches to chunked SSE framing and some clients send partial JSON fragments across SSE events causing our parser to choke.

liam: hypothesis 2: upstream proxy (nginx/nginx-plus) is buffering/terminating connections oddly under certain keepalive bursts — dropping mid-stream which causes truncated fragments. nginx error log shows `recv() failed (104: Connection reset by peer)` around same timestamps.

samir: another possibility: our SSE ingestion code expects full JSON in a single event when tool-call includes structured args. We missed a recent change in streaming parser to allow multi-event joins. See PR #1122.

maria: good. actions: 1) collect representative broken payloads to reproduce. 2) confirm client versions for impacted customers. 3) enable graceful reassembly in runtime as patch (short-term fallback). 4) consider throttling keepalive on proxy or increase timeouts.

aj: uploading sample payloads to /mnt/incident/2131110000/samples.tar.gz (shared link: https://files.redwood/paste/incident2131110000). Included a minimal curl reproduction with chunked SSE.

devon: repro attempt with curl -N against staging: if I send two small fragments separated by delays, our parser errors. Repro steps:
```bash
# sender (simulate client)
echo -ne \"data: {\\\"tool\\\": \\\"x\\\",\\\"args\\\": {\\\"q\\\": \\\"a\\\"}}\"
# cut here to simulate chunk
sleep 0.5
echo -ne \"}\\n\\n\" | nc -l 8080
# receiver
curl -N http://localhost:8080/stream
```
Observed: parser raises unexpected EOF and connection closes.

liam: proxy config snippet (from prod):
```
proxy_read_timeout 60s;
proxy_send_timeout 60s;
keepalive_timeout 75s 15s;
client_header_timeout 10s;
```
No obvious culprit but we saw a lot of `502`/`upstream prematurely closed connection` between 11:23-11:27.

maria: running quick mitigation: 1) flip runtime to tolerant-parsing=true on canary (us-east-1) and route 20% traffic there. 2) notify customers with known SDK 2.14.x to roll back to 2.13.x for the moment. 3) add temporary ingress rule to increase client_header_timeout to 30s.

samir: patch for tolerant parsing ready: small change in parser to buffer across SSE events until JSON validated. Applied to canary container image `redwood/runtime:213111-canary`.

aj: canary up at 11:41 UTC. Metrics: tool-call parse_errors in canary reduced to 0.2% within 10m. Non-canary remains ~8.7%.

maria: good progress. escalation: PagerDuty notes we hit customer-impact threshold for 3 customers. sr-level notified. Need a post-incident communication draft after stable.

liam: infrastructure note: there were connection flaps on a single proxy instance host ip 10.1.2.45 during the window; kernel logs show `rst` bursts correlated with noisy process (high CPU). Might be unrelated but tracking.

devon: collecting HTTP traces and raw SSE frames from edge logs to confirm fragmentation pattern. Uploading to incident bucket.

samir: hypothesis ranking so far: 1) client SDK change + parser strictness (HIGH), 2) proxy premature connection close amplifying fragments (MED), 3) unrelated kernel-level RSTs causing some drops (LOW).

maria: decision: promote tolerant-parsing to 100% in us-east-1 at 11:55 after verifying no regressions. Also schedule a formal rollback path.

aj: promoted. Observed global parse_errors across region drop from 8.2% -> 0.4% in 10 minutes. Streaming disconnect rate also down from 12% -> 2.1%.

pagerduty-bot: Incident status: mitigation successful. Pager duty alerts silenced. Incident owner: maria.

maria: next steps before RCA: 1) gather all logs and timelines (I’ll compile), 2) work with SDK team to publish hotfix or compatibility note, 3) schedule a deeper postmortem to test parser change across clients and add unit tests for multi-event JSON reassembly.

liam: also propose we add an ingress synthetic test that streams fragmented JSON to validate.

devon: adding an e2e test in CI that simulates SSE fragmentation + tool-calls. I’ll open PR and link in the postmortem.

samir: leaving notes for RCA doc: timeline, sample payloads, kernel host 10.1.2.45, proxy logs, canary image tag, mitigation timestamps, affected customer list (A, C, D — redacted).

maria: thanks team. I’ll create the incident timeline doc and drop link here for RCA. Marking this thread resolved for live mitigation; keep replies for RCA evidence collection. :white_check_mark:
